heading: Decentralized where it is priced, not where it is kept honest
lede: Decentralization is not one property a design either has or lacks — it is a choice about which specific part of a system is allowed to act on its own, and which part exists to reconcile what the independent parts did. HEZE's docket makes that choice explicitly rather than picking a slogan.

grid.p: Each door issues against its own local share of a tranche, on its own schedule, with no door needing another door's permission to move.
Two of three custodians per syndicate sign before anything is real, and every door's events are reconciled into one chain the syndicate keeps.
200 doors with no reconciliation would drift apart with no way to catch a contradiction. One central authority with no independent doors would only ever be checking itself.

note.text: It is not a claim that nobody is in charge — two of three custodians signing is a real, named authority, on purpose. It is a claim about where that authority sits: at the reconciliation, not at any one door, and never in one signature alone.

text: Decentralization taught as a specific design choice: which part of HEZE's docket acts independently (the doors) and which part reconciles (the syndicates), rather than an abstract slogan.
